short: Milites (latin) «servicemen, soldiers» were trained regular infantrymen in the Roman army, and later this term was also used to describe «soldiers» in Medieval Europe. Milites are set in contrast to tirones (latin tiro, tironis), recruits in the armies of the Roman Empire. In this status they were until six months after joining the legion, and only after completing the training, began to be considered milites - regular legionnaires. Details about the recruitment procedures for tirones in the army, the requirements for them and their training are described by Vegetius. The new recruits were trained not only in using various types of weapons, but also in long marches, the ability to keep formation and build fortifications, as well as other skills. Milites are another type of military unit whose presence is attested in the frontier districts. In the lists of troops of the Danubian provinces, they are listed together with the legions, and it is also stated that their commanders, as well as those of the frontier legions, were the prefects. This fact may indicate a close connection between the Milites and the Limitanei legions. Other evidence of such links are the coincidences in the unit names of both groups of troops. Ammianus Marcellinus calls them simply milites stationarii (Amm., XVIII, 5, 3; XXI, 3, 5).
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
